formats.title: Essentials · minimum practice
paragraphs: The shortest and most affordable format, well suited to individual engineers and students working with a very limited budget.
Also recommended when you need to learn a specific tool or a narrowly defined topic without covering the full course programme.
Practice is kept to a minimum: focused demonstrations and short exercises help you get started quickly.
formats.enquiry: 2 days of compact training with minimum practice, covering the essentials or specific topics agreed with your instructor.

formats.title: In-depth training · more practice
paragraphs: Recommended for companies that need to train their engineers even though training was not planned and no dedicated budget was set aside.

Five days allow a more thorough study of your chosen course, with substantially more guided practice, repetition and instructor feedback than the 2-day option. A practical choice when the full 10-day training and implementation programme is beyond the available budget.
formats.enquiry: 5 days of in-depth training with substantially more guided practice than the 2-day format.

formats.title: Training + your own pilot project
formats.split: 5 days of training + 5 days of guided project work
paragraphs: Designed for a full rollout of Tekla Structures in an engineering or detailing department. Your team works on a real project of your own and produces project drawings and other documentation with your instructor’s guidance.
The longer format allows topics to be explored in greater depth, with substantially more hands-on practice and time to resolve issues on your first project.
During the five-day pilot project, your instructor can also give additional lessons on specific topics relevant to your work, tailoring the training to your team’s needs.
formats.popularity: Around 95% of our clients choose training with a pilot project.
formats.enquiry: 5 days of in-depth training + 5 days on the customer’s own pilot project, producing project documentation with instructor support and additional targeted lessons as needed.

agreementClauses.title: Service and scope
agreementClauses.text: The supplier provides live online training in Tekla Structures for the customer’s nominated participants. The selected courses, group sizes, durations and fees are recorded in the order schedule. The selected course programmes attached to the commercial proposal define the training scope. Courses listed as optional are excluded.

agreementClauses.title: Training format
agreementClauses.text: Each training day represents eight teaching hours. A two-day format concentrates on essential or agreed focused topics with minimum practice. A five-day format provides substantially more guided practice. A ten-day format combines five days of training with five days of guided work on the customer’s own pilot project, including further focused explanations where needed.

agreementClauses.title: Dates and delivery
agreementClauses.text: Training is delivered online using Zoom, Google Meet or another agreed service. Desired start and end dates in the order are provisional. The parties confirm the teaching schedule, time zone and connection method separately in writing. Agreement of dates does not change the fees for the purchased course duration and group size.

agreementClauses.title: Fees and payment
agreementClauses.text: Payment is made by bank transfer against the supplier’s pro forma invoice. The agreed amount, currency, tax treatment and payment reference are stated in that document. The invoice is valid for six calendar months from its issue date; the expiry date is printed on the document. Payment terms are agreed separately. A downloaded pro forma invoice is not proof that payment has been received.

agreementClauses.title: Preparation and customer responsibilities
agreementClauses.text: Before the first lesson, the customer ensures that each participant has a suitable computer, a working connection and the required legally licensed software. The supplier helps with preparation in advance so paid lesson time is used for learning. The customer arranges any internal IT permissions and shared folders. Software licences are not included in the training fee.

agreementClauses.title: Pilot project and professional decisions
agreementClauses.text: Where pilot-project work is included, the customer supplies its own project materials and confirms that these may be used during training. The instructor helps the participants apply Tekla Structures workflows and prepare project documentation. The customer retains responsibility for engineering decisions, project checks and formal approval of the documentation.

agreementClauses.title: Certificates and follow-up support
agreementClauses.text: After completing the training, each participant receives a personalised electronic TopEngineer certificate with a unique number and the course duration. Participants may print their own paper copies. Brief follow-up questions that do not require substantial instructor time may be answered free of charge. More involved assistance is a separate service, with the task and hourly rate agreed before work starts.

agreementClauses.title: Confidential materials
agreementClauses.text: The parties use project files and business information supplied for training only for delivering and administering the agreed service, unless another use is authorised in writing. Customer project materials are not used for public promotion without the customer’s consent.

agreementClauses.title: Changes, cancellation and rescheduling
agreementClauses.text: Rescheduling the training does not change the training fee. If the customer requests a refund, the supplier refunds the payment less bank commissions. No other cancellation fee is deducted. Changes to the selected courses, duration or group size require an updated quotation.

agreementClauses.title: Final review and execution
agreementClauses.text: This template is a draft for review. The parties must confirm the final legal terms, applicable law and dispute-resolution provisions before signature. The website does not sign this document on behalf of either party. The customer’s request to prepare documents is not acceptance of an unsigned draft agreement.
